rationale: Block 4 completes the chemical hierarchy from base to nucleotide; these blanks test recall of the structural terms and distinctions that underpin all subsequent molecular biology.

Block 6 details the atomic sources of the purine ring; dragging each source into its position tests recall of this high-yield table and reinforces the metabolic connections to amino acid and folate pathways.
Block 7 traces purine catabolism step by step to uric acid; ordering these statements tests understanding of the pathway sequence that explains gout and the action of allopurinol.
Block 9 establishes the mechanics of replication at the fork; these blanks test recall of the key enzymes and structural features that distinguish leading from lagging strand synthesis.

Block 11 describes the properties of the genetic code and translation mechanics; marking the defining properties in running prose tests whether students can distinguish these key terms from surrounding description.

Block 13 introduces four distinct DNA repair pathways each matched to a characteristic lesion type; dragging the pathway name onto a schematic of its lesion tests visual recognition of the repair logic.
Block 14 explains gene regulation from the lac operon to eukaryotic epigenetics; these blanks test recall of the key regulatory molecules and mechanisms that control when genes are turned on or off.

Block 20 explains PCR as a three-step thermal cycle central to modern diagnostics; ordering visually distinct stages tests understanding of the logic behind each temperature shift and its molecular event.
